_about: A NEW VALLEY EVERY GAME (WORLD 6, rule 318, ask line 315; Paolo 11/2: 'I am not getting big procedurally generated map vibes at all... the Remnants are on the same part of the map... I don't even know if you have a number seed system'). ONE CAMPAIGN SEED, a short code shown on the new-game screen and saved with the game, decides WHO stands on the land; the land itself (Las Vegas's streets, freeways, mountains, passes and the real places the valley generator seats from the fixed land seed 'bohemia') never moves. Battle Brothers is the reference: every campaign is a world generated from a seed you can see and type in. Read by engine/bohemia_world_seed.js (node) and inlined into slices/BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html as BOHEMIA_WORLD_SEED_DATA (the page); gates/a_new_valley_every_game_gate.js refuses a drift between the two. Every number here is ours, draft, for TUNING's table.

same_seed_same_world.quote: Generated map layouts are stored in map seeds. Starting a new campaign with a same map seed will always generate the same map including locations and their named items

typed_and_shared.quote: Added map seed that can be entered upon starting a new campaign, and seen for ongoing campaigns created after this update, for replaying and sharing maps.

a_word_not_a_number.quote: Changed map seed to use words made up of characters from a to z, and no longer exclusively numbers in hexadecimal notation.

code.alphabet_why: no 0, O, 1, I or L: a code read off a phone and typed into another phone must not have two letters that look the same

older_saves_keep_their_world.source: the same 1415 quote: 'seen for ongoing campaigns created after this update'
older_saves_keep_their_world.ours: a campaign begun before the seed has no code and keeps the old valley

classic.name: THE OLD VALLEY
classic.why: a game saved before the seed existed, and the checkers' bench (the dark lifted), keep the fourteen bases where they always stood (CT_BASES_BAKED in the map): never move a base under a saved game

spread.min_apart_why: blocks, the longer side: two capitals never share a neighbourhood. A fortress's ground is 4 blocks wide, so 9 leaves a street of somebody else's between any two towns. Measured on the old layout: four bases (the Volunteers, the Network, the Reds, the Mob) stood within 6 blocks of each other in the north, the Volunteers and the Network 3 apart
spread.floor_apart_why: the spacing is relaxed to this, never below, when a faction's real places are all crowded; two town grounds never touch
spread.edge_inset_why: a town on the valley's last rows is clipped by the map's edge (faction_between M2); a preference, dropped only when the faction's only real places are at the edge
spread.density_why: a capital with nobody around it is a faction with no members (people join by nearness to a base, engine/bohemia_towns.js placeHomes): a place is weighted by how much town is within 8 blocks of it, softened (the square root), so a seed leans to a living street but the truck stop at the valley's south edge still wins its share. Measured at 1.0: the truck stop won 1 seed in 10 against a weight of 4
spread.one_place_one_ticket: blocks of one kind that touch are ONE place (the prison is three blocks, the warehouses two): a seed picks the place, then a block of it. Measured before: the Remnants' three prison blocks drew three tickets and stood in the east in 8 seeds of 10
spread.order_why: the faction with the fewest real places picks first, so a seed never leaves the Network (one radio mast, two substations, the tower, the sign) without a home because somebody else's base stood too close

Remnants.real: the air base, the prisons and the jail: where men with guns and orders stayed

Network.real: the radio mast, the tower on the Strip, the substations, the big sign: a psyop needs a transmitter
Network.note: Only faction with a manufactured origin.

Cartel.real: the storage yards, warehouses, the terminal and the swap meet: where it would hold ground, on the supply line
Cartel.note: Organized human predation. Supply chains mirror caravan routes.

Caravans.real: the truck stop, the terminal, the warehouses and the yards

Church.real: the chapels, the cemeteries, a school gym for the flock

Reds.real: downtown, the courthouses, the malls: where the money was counted
Reds.note: Economic engine, compound-interest faction. Not military.

Blues.real: the parks and the water parks: green ground and water

Trades.real: the industrial blocks, the battery plant, the warehouses

Volunteers.real: the hospitals, the campus, the schools, the library

Homeless.real: the pump station over the flood tunnels, the trailer parks, the storage lots
Homeless.note: Sewer/tunnel HQ under the King Hobo.

Anarchists.real: squats: dead apartment blocks, strip malls, trailer lots

Colorful.real: a neighbourhood that looks after itself

Custom.real: the player's own outfit: any street that will have it
Custom.note: No preset philosophy; it is the player's.

min_places_why: and at least three separate places (touching blocks of one kind are one place), or a faction with three prison blocks is a faction with one home
min_sites_why: every faction has at least three real places it could stand on in the valley, or the seed is a fixed seat with extra steps; the gate counts them on the real map

start.why: the same seed and the same origin start in the same corner and the same town (the corner used to be a dice roll off the clock, so a shared seed could not share a start)

left_for_later: who holds the region's twelve outer towns (region_bases.json holders): the page never hands that file to the home-base ledger (setRegion is node-only), so there is nothing to seed until RUN wires it
the region's camps and lairs (hostile_locations): each stands at one named real place with no candidate list yet
what is looted or burned at the start, the shops' stock rolls, the crew's roll
